example_limits: Original project earliest-finish estimator, not a production scheduler. Python 3.11+ functools.cache remembers completed recursive task results within a fresh estimator-owned immutable tuple snapshot. Well-formed duration/dependency pairs are copied without concurrent edits; durations are nonnegative integers and every prerequisite must refer to an earlier task. Public indices validated before cache access, including rejecting bool/negative/out-of-range values. Unlimited parallel resources and fixed integer-minute durations are assumed. Five-task graph durations 2,3,4,1,2 and dependency lists empty,[0],[0],[1,2],[3] yields finishes 2,5,6,7,9. First root call has five misses and one shared-task hit; uncached recursion would run six task bodies. Calling package afterward does no additional body work. Input edit task0=20 leaves old snapshot root9; fresh estimator root27. Clear empties entries while retaining the original frozen input; handles retain the snapshot until released/collectible. Cache has no automatic size bound but validated finite task indices bound entries per estimator. No network, database, persistence, cross-process sharing, cancellation, concurrent scheduling, single-flight guarantee, TTL or live project refresh. Original React editor context is explanatory only; no React code or dependency added. Memoisation is a spelling alias. The original memo-function paper is historical foundation; modern memoization, top-down dynamic programming, bottom-up tabulation, Cache-Aside and Flyweight remain distinguished.
